Submitted electronically to www.regulations.gov 
 
June 2, 2026 
 
Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. 
Secretary, Department of Health and Human Services 
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services  
Department of Health and Human Services  
Attention: CMS-0062-P 
P.O. Box 8013 
Baltimore, MD 21244-8013 
 
Re: Comments on CMS-0062-P Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Patient Protection and Affordable 
Care Act; Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs for Medicare Advantage 
Organizations, Medicaid Managed Care Plans, State Medicaid Agencies, Childrenâ€™s Health Insurance 
Program (CHIP) Agencies and CHIP Managed Care Entities, and Issuers of Qualified Health Plans on 
the Federally-Facilitated Exchanges. 
 
Dear Secretary Kennedy, 
VGM & Associates, Inc. (VGM) appreciates the opportunity to submit comments on the Centers for 
Medicare and Medicaid Servicesâ€™ (CMSâ€™) Request for Information cited above. VGM is a nationwide 
member services organization representing DMEPOS suppliers, distributors, manufacturers and other 
industry stakeholders, all of whom play a crucial role in the health care continuum ensuring Medicare 
beneficiaries receive the products and services they need to remain in their homes. 
 
How do prior authorization requirements for laboratory tests and DMEPOS items currently impact patient 
care and health care provider burden?  
Prior authorization requirements increase the administrative burden for providers resulting in delays in 
access to care for patients. The following is just one example that clearly illustrates the impact of prior 
authorization requirements for DMEPOS items to the detriment of patient outcomes. 
Numerous wheelchair components and replacement power mobility devices require prior authorization 
before the beneficiaryâ€™s wheelchair can be repaired or replaced. When the wheelchair serves as the sole 
means of mobility for the beneficiary and the prior authorization process can take up to 30 days, the 
beneficiary may find themselves without their wheelchair for six to eight weeks or longer.  The process 
requires the provider conduct an assessment to identify the problem and the necessary repairs or to 
determine if replacement is more prudent. Subsequently, the treating practitioner must document the 
DMEPOS item being repaired/replaced remains reasonable and necessary within six months prior to the 
repair/replacement. 
In addition, either the treating practitioner or the supplier must confirm the repair itself is reasonable and 
necessary, if repair is the least costly alternative and the power mobility device is repairable. Only after 
this documentation is obtained and prior authorization is granted, can the supplier order the parts or 
replacement chair. After the beneficiary has waited for the paperwork and parts/replacement chair, they 
can then arrange for the repair or fitting /delivery of the new power mobility device. The duration of this 
process not only has detrimental physical effects on the beneficiary but also adversely impacts their 
 
 
mental well-being. During this waiting period, the beneficiary experiences limited mobility and lacks 
access to medical appointments and other essential activities outside their home. This waiting period 
could be cut in half (three to four weeks) if prior authorization was not required for the repairs. 
In many instances, the individuals who rely on a power mobility device are in college or are working 
individuals who are unable to attend regular on campus classes or work while waiting for the necessary 
repairs or replacement. These individuals often develop pressure sores from being bed confined and 
ultimately become depressed and anxious while waiting on access to care and mobility to regain their 
independence. 
Due to the extensive impact prior authorization has on patients in many instances, VGM recommends 
CMS only require prior authorization in instances where repairs to DMEPOS equipment are not possible 
and new equipment is necessary. VGM also recommends requiring the repair quote demonstrating that 
replacement is the more cost-effective solution. Doing so supports the Administrationâ€™s initiative to 
reduce waste and would expedite the service to the patient. 
 
What opportunities for process improvement exist for prior authorization requirements? Are changes 
needed to make requirements even more effective at containing costs, reducing burden, and improving 
patient outcomes?  
Prior authorization serves to ensure medical necessity and is generally supported by VGM. However, 
there are instances where a patientâ€™s condition clearly indicates medical necessity and the delay in 
service to the patient due to the back and forth required to obtain prior authorization is overly 
burdensome and unnecessary. To contain costs, reduce administrative burden and improve patient 
outcomes, VGM recommends CMS identify a list of specific diagnoses whereby prior authorization 
would be automatically approved. For example, patients with quadriplegia should receive automatic 
authorization approval for certain DMEPOS items. 
 
How could automation of the prior authorization process for laboratory tests and DMEPOS items positively 
affect patient outcomes and potentially reduce both payer and health care provider burden?  
Automation will facilitate quicker access to care for patients, which would enhance health outcomes and 
minimize complications. Automation guarantees that essential care is not delayed due to administrative 
mistakes. The enhanced patient experience resulting from the automation of prior authorization will lead 
to reduced waiting times, fewer cancellations of assessments and procedures, and more reliable 
scheduling, along with diminished anxiety stemming from uncertainty and delays. 
Automation will also alleviate administrative burden on healthcare providers by removing manual tasks 
such as fax submissions, phone calls, and repetitive data entry. Additionally, automation can optimize 
workflow by integrating directly with EMR systems allowing for one-click submissions. Consequently, 
these efficiencies will help reduce staff burnout and turnover, lead to fewer denials and appeals, 
resulting in reduced provider burden. 
Further, automation also benefits the Medicare program by enhancing transparency and providing 
insight into utilization patterns and approval trends. Such insights can inform better policy decisions and 
care pathways. 
VGM recommends CMS implement automation of the prior authorization process with safeguards in place 
to ensure supported medically necessary prior authorizations are processed quickly and efficiently. 
 
 
 
How do the issues associated with prior authorization impact the health care workforce and retention of 
skilled health care professionals 
Prior authorization requirements greatly increase the non-clinical workload on the health care workforce. 
Providers submit numerous prior authorization requests each week, often dedicating at least one full-
time FTE, if not several depending on the size of the practice, to prior authorization responsibilities. 
Providers are often required to recruit extra personnel solely to manage prior authorization 
documentation, which adds to operational complexity and increased expense.  The administrative tasks 
associated with prior authorization are understood as one of the primary sources of inefficiencies within 
clinical workflows. 
Prior authorization requirements redirect time and resources away from patient care, leading to 
diminished professional workforce satisfaction and productivity. Providers and their workforce frequently 
experience burnout and emotional fatigue, which fosters frustration and disengagement. Prior 
authorization requirements involve repetitive documentation and appeals management which often 
require the work to extend beyond regular hours (including evenings and weekends), exacerbating 
workforce fatigue and disrupted work-life balance. Burnout results in emotional fatigue, diminished 
resilience, and lower job satisfactionâ€”critical indicators of turnover in the health care workforce. 
Decreased job satisfaction negatively impacts retention and makes health care careers less appealing 
to newcomers, intensifying long-term staffing issues. 
  
VGM appreciates the opportunity to comment on proposed rule CMS-0062-P and welcomes continued 
dialogue and to provide additional information. I may be reached at mike.isaacson@vgm.com.   
Sincerely, 
 
Michael Isaacson  
Senior Vice President, Government & Regulatory Relations
analysis:
## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** VGM & Associates, Inc.; signed by Michael Isaacson, Senior Vice President, Government & Regulatory Relations.
- **Stakeholder type:** Professional Association
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** Nationwide member services organization representing DMEPOS suppliers, distributors, manufacturers, and industry stakeholders.

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

VGM responds to CMS's RFI on DMEPOS prior authorization, arguing that PA creates significant delays and burden, especially for wheelchair repairs and replacements. It recommends limiting PA for repairs to cases where repair is impossible and replacement is needed, creating automatic authorization for specified diagnoses, automating PA with safeguards and EMR integration, and reducing workforce burden caused by repetitive documentation, appeals, and staffing needs.

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** GENERAL/RFI; API-USAGE-METRICS by analogy to automation transparency.
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** CMS-0062-P.
- **Standards referenced:** Automation; EMR integration; no specific FHIR or NCPDP standards.

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: DMEPOS PA burden and wheelchair repairs**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** PA for wheelchair components and power mobility repairs/replacements can leave beneficiaries without mobility for six to eight weeks or longer.
- **Specific request:** Require PA only where repairs are not possible and new equipment is necessary.

**Topic 2: Cost-effective repair/replacement review**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Documentation and PA should focus on whether repair is feasible and least costly, without delaying necessary mobility restoration.
- **Specific request:** Require a repair quote showing replacement is the more cost-effective solution when replacement is sought.

**Topic 3: Automatic authorization for clear diagnoses**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Some conditions clearly establish medical necessity, making back-and-forth PA unnecessary.
- **Specific request:** Create a list of diagnoses eligible for automatic authorization, such as quadriplegia for specified DMEPOS items.

**Topic 4: Automation of DMEPOS PA**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Support/Modify
- **Rationale:** Automation can reduce waiting times, cancellations, administrative mistakes, fax/phone/repetitive entry, denials, appeals, burnout, and turnover.
- **Specific request:** Implement automated PA with safeguards to quickly process supported medically necessary requests and integrate with EMRs for one-click submissions.

**Topic 5: Workforce impact**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** PA creates non-clinical workload, requires added FTEs, extends work after hours, and worsens burnout and retention.
- **Specific request:** Reduce PA burden and automate processes to improve workforce satisfaction and retention.

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S66-S82:** VGM directly responds to the DMEPOS RFI on patient care, provider burden, process improvement, automation, and workforce retention.
- **S29/S35:** By analogy, VGM notes automation can provide transparency into utilization patterns and approval trends, though it does not address proposed drug API metrics directly.

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Limit DMEPOS PA for repairs to cases where repair is not possible and replacement is necessary.
2. Require repair quotes demonstrating replacement is more cost-effective when applicable.
3. Identify diagnoses that should receive automatic authorization for specific DMEPOS items.
4. Implement automated DMEPOS PA with safeguards for medically necessary requests.
5. Integrate automation with EMR systems to support one-click submissions.
6. Use automation data to understand utilization patterns and approval trends.
7. Reduce repetitive documentation and appeals burden to support workforce retention.

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** DMEPOS PA delays, mobility loss, excessive documentation, workforce burnout, repetitive appeals, and operational costs.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Six-to-eight-week wheelchair delays, inability to attend school/work/medical appointments, pressure sores, depression, anxiety, loss of independence, burnout, turnover, and reduced workforce appeal.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Manual fax/phone/data entry, documentation requirements within six months, parts ordering after PA, repetitive appeals, and need for dedicated FTEs.

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** Wheelchair repair/replacement PA can leave beneficiaries without a wheelchair for six to eight weeks or longer; without PA for repairs, waiting periods could be cut to three to four weeks.
- **Studies or research referenced:** None.
- **Examples provided:** Power mobility device repairs/replacements, wheelchair components, quadriplegia, college/working beneficiaries, pressure sores from being bed confined.

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** Medicare beneficiaries using DMEPOS, DMEPOS suppliers, distributors, manufacturers, providers, staff, payers, and CMS.
- **Economic implications:** Automatic approvals and repair-focused policies may reduce waste and administrative costs; PA staffing adds operational expense.
- **Technical feasibility:** VGM supports automation with EMR integration and safeguards.
- **Patient care impact:** High for mobility-dependent beneficiaries; delays can cause health, mental health, employment, education, and independence harms.

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Concerned and reform-oriented
- **Tone:** Professional, operational, patient-impact focused
- **Priority level:** High

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "The beneficiary may find themselves without their wheelchair for six to eight weeks or longer." - Context: DMEPOS PA impact.
2. "VGM recommends CMS only require prior authorization in instances where repairs to DMEPOS equipment are not possible." - Context: Core recommendation.
3. "Automation will facilitate quicker access to care for patients." - Context: Automation support.
4. "Prior authorization requirements greatly increase the non-clinical workload on the health care workforce." - Context: Workforce impact.

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **COST-RESOURCES** - Discusses operational expense, FTEs, waste reduction, and repair/replacement cost-effectiveness.
- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** - PA documentation and appeals burden providers and suppliers.
- [x] **HEALTH-EQUITY** - Mobility-dependent beneficiaries face serious access and independence harms.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - Supports automation and EMR integration.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** - Focuses on timely access to mobility equipment.
- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** - Automation may provide utilization and approval trend insight.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - Critiques current manual PA, repair assessment, documentation, ordering, and appeals workflows.
- [x] **VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM** - DMEPOS suppliers, distributors, and manufacturers are directly affected.
